title: Judging a Physio Claim on Social Media or in an Advert — Seven Red Flags

hook.en: "Fix your sciatica in 3 minutes!" "The one stretch doctors do not want you to know." Every day, patients and students see claims like these, with big numbers and happy faces. You do not need a research degree to question them. Seven red flags and three plain questions will get you most of the way.
hook.ur: "Sciatica 3 minute mein theek karein!" "Woh ek stretch jo doctors aap ko nahi batana chahte." Har din mareez aur talba aise daawe bade numbers aur khush chehron ke saath dekhte hain. Un par sawal uthane ke liye research ki degree nahi chahiye. Saat red flags aur teen saade sawal aap ko zyada tar manzil tak pohancha dete hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll spot seven red flags in a health claim, ask three questions of any claim, check a source in two minutes, and respond kindly to a patient who shows you a viral video.
goal.ur: End tak aap sehat ke daawe mein saat red flags pehchanenge, kisi bhi daawe se teen sawal poochhenge, do minute mein zariya jaanchenge, aur viral video dikhane wale mareez ko narmi se jawab denge.

text.en: Health misinformation is common on social media and often spreads faster than careful information, because it is simple, emotional and sells hope. The **seven red flags**: (1) a **miracle or quick cure**, (2) **secret or "they don't want you to know"** language, (3) **before-and-after photos or testimonials as proof**, (4) **no sources, or cherry-picked ones**, (5) **the person sells the solution**, (6) **attacks on mainstream care or conspiracy talk**, and (7) **absolute certainty or fear** ("guaranteed", "100 percent", "you will end up crippled"). Add three questions: **Compared with what? How do they know? What do they gain?**
text.ur: Social media par sehat ki ghalat maloomat aam hai aur aksar ehtiyat se di gayi maloomat se tez phailti hai, kyunke woh saadi, jazbati aur ummeed bechti hai. **Saat red flags**: (1) **mojiza ya jaldi ilaaj**, (2) **raaz ya "woh aap ko batana nahi chahte"** ki zubaan, (3) **pehle aur baad ki tasveerein ya gawahiyan saboot ke taur par**, (4) **koi zariya nahi, ya chunindah zarai**, (5) **shakhs hal bechta hai**, (6) **mainstream care par hamle ya sazish ki baatein**, aur (7) **mutlaq yaqeen ya khauf** ("zamanat", "100 fisad", "aap apahij ho jayenge"). Teen sawal jorein: **Kis ke muqabale mein? Unhein kaise pata? Unhein kya milta hai?**

text.en: Think of **a street vendor selling a magic oil**. He shouts, shows a smiling customer, says doctors hide the secret and sells the bottle himself. A good pharmacist does none of these: he explains, shows the evidence, admits limits and does not pressure. The red flags are the vendor's tricks.
text.ur: **Sadak par jadui tel bechne wala** sochein. Woh chilata hai, muskurata gahak dikhata hai, kehta hai doctors raaz chhupate hain aur botal khud bechta hai. Achha pharmacist in mein se kuch nahi karta: samjhata hai, saboot dikhata hai, hadein maanta hai aur dabao nahi daalta. Red flags us bechne wale ki chaalein hain.

title.en: Seven red flags and the honest alternative
title.ur: Saat red flags aur imaandar mutabadil

rows.ur: 1. Mojiza ya jaldi ilaaj
"3 minute mein peeth dard hamesha ke liye theek"

rows.en: "Most back pain improves over weeks, and this may help some people"
rows.ur: "Zyada tar peeth dard haftoon mein behtar hota hai, aur yeh kuch logon ki madad kar sakta hai"
2. Raaz ka ilm
"Woh chaal jo doctors aap se chhupate hain"
Khule zarai jinhein koi bhi jaanch sakta hai
3. Tasveerein aur gawahiyan saboot ke taur par
"Ahmed ke pehle aur baad dekhein!"

rows.en: Comparison groups, numbers and how many did not improve
rows.ur: Comparison groups, numbers aur kitne behtar nahi hue
4. Zariye nahi ya chunindah
"Studies dikhati hain..." bina link ke

rows.en: A named study or review, with its size and limits
rows.ur: Naam wali study ya review, size aur hadon ke saath
5. Bechne wala hi zariya

rows.en: The same person sells the course, the device or the supplement
rows.ur: Wohi shakhs course, aala ya supplement bechta hai

rows.en: Declared interests, and advice that costs nothing as well
rows.ur: Batayey gaye mufaadat, aur mashwara jo muft bhi ho
6. Hamle aur sazish
"Doctors aur bari dawa companies jhoot bolte hain"

rows.en: Respect for other views, with reasons
rows.ur: Doosre nuqta-e-nazar ka ehtiram, wajuhaat ke saath
7. Yaqeen ya khauf

rows.en: "100 percent guaranteed" or "do this or be crippled"
rows.ur: "100 fisad zamanat" ya "yeh karo warna apahij"

rows.en: "It depends, and here is what we do not know"
rows.ur: "Yeh mukhtalif hota hai, aur yeh hai jo hum nahi jaante"

question.en: A video says, "This one exercise cures sciatica for good, with 100 percent success. Click the link to buy my course." How many red flags can you spot?
question.ur: Video kehta hai, "Yeh ek exercise sciatica hamesha ke liye theek karti hai, 100 fisad kamyabi ke saath. Mera course khareedne ke liye link dabayein." Aap kitne red flags pehchan sakte hain?

text.en: None; it sounds confident, so it must be true
text.ur: Koi nahi; yaqeen se bolta hai isliye sach hoga

text.en: At least three: a miracle cure, absolute certainty and the seller is the source
text.ur: Kam az kam teen: mojiza ilaaj, mutlaq yaqeen aur bechne wala hi zariya hai

feedback.en: Yes — more flags mean more caution.
feedback.ur: Haan — zyada flags ka matlab zyada ehtiyat.

question.en: A famous influencer shows ten patients who improved after using a device. Why is this weak evidence?
question.ur: Mashhoor influencer ek aale ke baad behtar hone wale das mareez dikhata hai. Yeh kamzor saboot kyun hai?

feedback.en: Some give good information; check each claim.
feedback.ur: Kuch achhi maloomat dete hain; har daawa jaanchein.

text.en: There is no comparison group, we do not see those who did not improve, and many conditions improve by themselves
text.ur: Comparison group nahi, jo behtar nahi hue woh nazar nahi aate, aur bohat si halatein khud behtar ho jati hain

feedback.en: Yes — testimonials suffer from selective memory and natural recovery.
feedback.ur: Haan — gawahiyan chunindah yaadasht aur qudrati sehatyabi se mutasir hoti hain.

text.en: Ten is too many to be believable
text.ur: Das itne zyada hain ke qabil-e-yaqeen nahi

feedback.en: The number of cases is not the issue.

question.en: A patient shows you a viral video promising to fix her knee pain. What is the kindest, most useful response?
question.ur: Ek mareeza aap ko ek viral video dikhati hai jo ghutne ka dard theek karne ka waada karti hai. Sab se narm aur mufeed jawab kya hai?

text.en: Thank her for asking, look at the video together, point out what is sensible and what is overpromised, and agree what is safe to try
text.ur: Poochhne ka shukriya, video saath dekhein, batayein kya samajhdar hai aur kya zyada waada hai, aur tay karein kya aazmana mehfooz hai

feedback.en: Yes — curiosity and respect keep trust.
feedback.ur: Haan — tajassus aur izzat bharosa qaim rakhte hain.

text.en: Tell her she is foolish for believing it
text.ur: Kahein ke woh is par yaqeen kar ke bewaqoof hai

feedback.ur: Sharminda karna baat cheet band karta hai.

text.en: Ignore the video and change the subject
text.ur: Video nazar-andaaz kar ke mauzu badlein

feedback.en: She may try it anyway, unsupervised.
feedback.ur: Woh phir bhi bina nigrani aazma sakti hai.

text.en: **Believing that only fools fall for misinformation.** Clever, caring people share health claims because they want to help, and fear and pain make everyone want a quick fix. Do not shame people: ask what attracted them, check the claim together and offer a better option. And remember that some online health content is excellent, so check each source, not the platform.
text.ur: **Yeh samajhna ke sirf bewaqoof ghalat maloomat par yaqeen karte hain.** Samajhdar, dekhbhal karne wale log sehat ke daawe is liye share karte hain ke madad karna chahte hain, aur khauf aur dard har kisi ko jaldi hal ki khwahish dilate hain. Logon ko sharminda na karein: poochhein kya kheencha, daawa milkar jaanchein aur behtar option dein. Yeh bhi yaad rakhein ke kuch online sehat ka mawad shandar hai, isliye har zariya jaanchein, platform nahi.

text.en: **Teach patients a two-minute check.** Who is saying it? What are they selling? Where is the evidence, and is it from a trial or just stories? Does it say "compared with what"? Is it based on one study or on several? Print the seven red flags as a small card for your waiting room and offer to look at any claim a patient brings. Being open to the video is what lets you correct it.
text.ur: **Mareezon ko do minute ki jaanch sikhayein.** Kaun keh raha hai? Kya bech raha hai? Saboot kahan hai, aur kya trial se hai ya sirf kahaniyan? Kya "kis ke muqabale mein" kehta hai? Ek study par hai ya kai par? Saat red flags ka chhota card apne intezar gaah ke liye print karein aur kisi bhi daawe ko dekhne ki peshkash karein jo mareez laye. Video ke liye khula hona hi aap ko usay theek karne deta hai.

question.en: Why does misinformation spread faster than careful information?
question.ur: Ghalat maloomat ehtiyat se di gayi maloomat se tez kyun phailti hai?

answer.en: It is simple, emotional, novel and often tells a story with a villain and a hero, which is easy to share. Careful information has caveats ("it depends", "it helps a little"), which are less shareable. Platforms also reward engagement, not accuracy. The answer is not to be as dramatic, but to be clear, kind and quick: short videos with a plain message and a source, from people audiences trust.
answer.ur: Yeh saada, jazbati, naya hota hai aur aksar aisi kahani sunata hai jis mein villain aur hero ho, jo share karna aasaan hai. Ehtiyat wali maloomat mein sharaait hoti hain ("yeh mukhtalif hota hai", "thori madad karta hai"), jo kam share hoti hain. Platforms bhi engagement ko inaam dete hain, durusti ko nahi. Jawab itna dramatic hona nahi, balke saaf, narm aur tez hona hai: chhoti videos saade paigham aur zariye ke saath, un logon se jin par sunne wale bharosa karte hain.

beats.patient: A student sees a viral clip of a "master therapist" who says "foam rolling breaks up scar tissue and cures chronic pain forever," showing before-and-after photos and a link to his paid course. She is about to share it.
beats.assessment: Red flags: a miracle cure, absolute certainty, before-and-after photos as proof, no source and a seller who profits.
beats.treatment: She asks, "compared with what, and how does he know?", finds no study, searches a database where reviews suggest only small, short-lived effects on flexibility, and shares a short, kind correction instead.
beats.reassess: Her post helps classmates to question the claim, and one of them thanks her for saving money.

text.en: **Some misinformation is dangerous.** Claims that discourage medical care, such as telling people to stop medicines, avoid scans for serious symptoms or treat chest pain with a stretch, can cause harm. If a patient mentions such a claim, take it seriously, encourage them to speak to their doctor and make sure they know the warning signs that need urgent care. Report clearly dangerous content to the platform.
text.ur: **Kuch ghalat maloomat khatarnak hoti hai.** Aise daawe jo tibbi care se rokte hain, jaise dawaiyan band karne, seriyas alamaat par scan se bachne ya seene ke dard ko stretch se theek karne ko kehna, nuqsan kar sakte hain. Agar koi mareez aisa daawa zikr kare to isay seriyas lein, unhein apne doctor se baat karne ko kahein aur yaqeeni banayein ke unhein un khatre ki nishaniyon ka pata ho jin ko foran care chahiye. Saaf taur par khatarnak mawad platform ko report karein.

text.en: A systematic review of health misinformation on social media found that it was common, with the highest prevalence in posts about vaccines, drugs, smoking and eating disorders, and that it was more prevalent on some platforms than others, calling for better tools to identify and counter it. A review of trust and credibility in web-based health information described that people judge credibility using cues such as source reputation, design, writing quality and whether the information matches their beliefs, which means that attractive, confident presentation can persuade even when the content is weak.
text.ur: Social media par sehat ki ghalat maloomat ke ek systematic review ne paya ke yeh aam thi, vaccines, dawaon, cigarette aur khane ki bimariyon ke posts mein sab se zyada, aur ke kuch platforms par doosron se zyada thi, aur ise pehchanne aur is ka muqabla karne ke behtar aalon ka mutalba kiya. Web par sehat ki maloomat mein bharosa aur sakh ke review ne bayan kiya ke log sakh ka faisla zariye ki shohrat, design, tehreer ki quality aur is baat se karte hain ke maloomat un ke yaqeen se milti hain ya nahi, yani dilkash, pur-aitmaad pesh-kash kamzor mawad ke bawajood qaail kar sakti hai.

text.en: **Seven flags, Three questions.** Miracle, secret, testimonial, no source, seller, conspiracy, certainty; then: compared with what, how do they know, what do they gain?
text.ur: **Saat flags, Teen sawal.** Mojiza, raaz, gawahi, zariya nahi, bechne wala, sazish, yaqeen; phir: kis ke muqabale mein, unhein kaise pata, unhein kya milta hai?

summary.en: Seven red flags: miracle cure, secrecy, testimonials, no sources, a selling source, conspiracy talk and certainty or fear.
summary.ur: Saat red flags: mojiza ilaaj, raaz, gawahiyan, zariye nahi, bechne wala zariya, sazish ki baat aur yaqeen ya khauf.

summary.en: Ask: compared with what, how do they know, and what do they gain?
summary.ur: Poochhein: kis ke muqabale mein, unhein kaise pata, aur unhein kya milta hai?

summary.en: Respond to patients with curiosity, not shame, and take dangerous claims seriously.
summary.ur: Mareezon ko sharminda karne ke bajaye tajassus se jawab dein, aur khatarnak daawon ko seriyas lein.

front.ur: Sehat ke daawe mein teen red flags batayein.

back.en: Miracle cure, testimonials as proof, and a seller who profits.
back.ur: Mojiza ilaaj, saboot ke taur par gawahiyan, aur munafa kamane wala bechne wala.
